stem: For three commodities the base-year and current-year prices and quantities are: A: p0=6, q0=3, p1=14, q1=4; B: p0=4, q0=4, p1=2, q1=2; C: p0=8, q0=2, p1=10, q1=3. Which statement about the Fisher Ideal price index is correct?

options.text: It is 150, and it satisfies both the time reversal and factor reversal tests.
It is 140, and it satisfies both the time reversal and factor reversal tests.
It is about 160.71, and it satisfies the factor reversal test only.
It is about 150.36, and it satisfies both reversal tests.

per_option_rationale.rationale: Sum p1q0 = 70, p0q0 = 50, so Laspeyres = 140. Sum p1q1 = 90, p0q1 = 56, so Paasche = 160.71. Fisher = sqrt(140 * 160.71) = sqrt(22500) = 150. Fisher is the only common index that satisfies BOTH the time reversal and factor reversal tests, which is why it is called ideal.
Reports 140, which is the Laspeyres index alone (base-year quantities throughout). Fisher uses both quantity sets, and the test claim is attached to the wrong value.
Reports 160.71, the Paasche index alone (current-year quantities throughout), and wrongly limits the test property. Fisher satisfies both reversal tests, not only factor reversal.
Uses the arithmetic mean (140 + 160.71)/2 = 150.36 (the Dorbish-Bowley index) in place of Fisher's geometric mean. Fisher is the square root of the product, not the simple average.

explanation: Fisher is the geometric mean of Laspeyres and Paasche, so build both first. With base quantities: Laspeyres = (sum p1q0 / sum p0q0)*100 = (70/50)*100 = 140. With current quantities: Paasche = (sum p1q1 / sum p0q1)*100 = (90/56)*100 = 160.71. Fisher = sqrt(L*P) = sqrt(140 * 160.71) = sqrt(22500) = 150. The adequacy property: Fisher uniquely satisfies both the time reversal test (P01 * P10 = 1) and the factor reversal test (P01 * Q01 = value ratio), which is exactly why it is named the Ideal index.

explanation_sections.punchline: Fisher = geometric mean of Laspeyres and Paasche: sqrt(140 * 160.71) = sqrt(22500) = 150, and it is the index that satisfies both reversal tests.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula: Fisher = sqrt(Laspeyres * Paasche). Map givens by building four weighted sums, sum p1q0 and sum p0q0 for Laspeyres, sum p1q1 and sum p0q1 for Paasche. Compute L = 140, P = 160.71, then take the square root of their product, not the average. Recall the property: Fisher alone meets both time reversal and factor reversal, hence Ideal.
explanation_sections.lesson: Fisher is the geometric mean (square root of the product) of Laspeyres and Paasche, and it is the only common index satisfying both reversal tests.
explanation_sections.timing: About 170 seconds: four sums, two ratios, one square root, plus the property recall. Reject the 140 option in five seconds: that is Laspeyres alone, which ignores current-year quantities entirely.
